study_identification_part.si_4_title: Sex Determines Anterior Cingulate Cortex Cortical Thickness in the Course of Depression

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study employed two modeling approaches: (1) Linear mixed-effects (LME) models implemented with the 3dLMEr program within AFNI for the main group comparisons, with site as a random effect for both intercept and group; (2) Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) via PCNToolkit (version 0.18) for neuroanatomical normative modeling to capture individual-level variability in ACC cortical thickness and compute deviation z-scores.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To control for site-related confounding, we employed the linear mixed-effect (LME) model implemented with the 3dLMEr program within AFNI... Finally, to assess the within-group heterogeneity, we also applied neuroanatomical normative modeling to capture individual-level variability in ACC CT, performed within the PCNToolkit (version 0.18) package... Hierarchical Bayesian regression analysis was employed to accommodate intersite variation and generate normative models using the covariates of sex, age, and education.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Wu2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Statistical Analysis

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness (CT) of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and its subdivisions: dorsal ACC (dACC, BA24), subgenual ACC (sgACC, BA25), and pregenual ACC (pgACC, BA32). CT was estimated using the DiReCT (diffeomorphic registration-based cortical thickness) algorithm available in ANTs, with SPM12 segmentation as input.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Then, CT estimation was further performed by the DiReCT (diffeomorphic registration-based cortical thickness) algorithm available in ANTs (Advanced Normalization Tools)... We used the extended Human Connectome Project multimodal parcellation atlas of the human cortex and subcortical areas defining the ACC as Brodmann area (BA) 24 (dACC), BA 25 (sgACC), and BA 32 (pgACC).
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Wu2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Brain Imaging; Imaging Data

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: For the LME model: Age, sex, and education were included as fixed-effect covariates; site was included as a random effect for both intercept and group. For the normative modeling (HBR via PCNToolkit): sex, age, and education were used as covariates to generate normative models accommodating intersite variation.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In this model, the intercept and the group variable (first-episode MDD vs. recurrent MDD vs. HCs) contained random effects that were specific to site and fixed effects that were independent of site. Other variables were considered covariates of no interest. Given that sex- and age-related differences in the morphology of the CT have been reported [e.g., (14,42,43)] and that intelligence may influence CT [e.g., (44)], we added sex, age, and education as covariates in the analysis... Hierarchical Bayesian regression analysis was employed to accommodate intersite variation and generate normative models using the covariates of sex, age, and education.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Wu2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Statistical Analysis
